judul: A case study on the integration of a snapshot hyperspectral field-portable imager solving fruit quality assessment
sumber: Proceedings of SPIE the International Society for Optical Engineering
abstrak: This case study investigates the integration of a snapshot hyperspectral, field-portable imaging system for comprehensive fruit quality and yield assessment in agricultural orchards. The study introduces a novel framework for segmenting, counting, sizing, and estimating the ripeness of orchard fruit using spatial-spectral data. By combining hyperspectral imaging (HSI) with RGB data, we address the complexities of real-world agricultural environments, including occlusion, shadowing, and motion blur. Our proposed 1D-ConvNet + SAM2 model outperforms the RGB-only YOLOv8s approach, achieving a 25 percent improvement in recall by leveraging spectral data to detect partially occluded fruit. Using DepthAnythingV2 (DAv2), we estimate metric depth to localize fruit detections within a unified 3D coordinate system, enabling unique tracking and accurate fruit counting across video frames. This capability supports yield estimation by providing precise counts and sizes of individual fruits in the orchard. Furthermore, segmentation masks and point clouds derived from monocular depth estimation are employed for fruit sizing, with future work focusing on improving handling of occlusions and segmentation errors. In addition to spatial-spectral detection, we demonstrate the feasibility of non-destructive ripeness estimation by correlating spectral features in the fruit’s skin with sugar content. An in-lab experiment using the Living Optics hyperspectral camera achieved a Brix correlation with an R2 of 0.71, underscoring the potential of HSI for assessing ripeness and fruit quality. This research highlights the utility of snapshot hyperspectral imaging as an all-in-one solution for end-to-end fruit quality and yield assessment in orchards. The dataset used in this study is publicly available at https: //huggingface.co/datasets/LivingOptics/hyperspectral-orchard, encouraging further advancements in agricultural hyperspectral imaging and computer vision.
